answer: Copying the same citations across 229 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 229 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the sparrow index resolves every citation against the falcon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the garden audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 682 identities would post 3853 proofs and burn roughly 64 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
